newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Naphtha down on prompt supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Naphtha down on prompt supplies.

text.p: Asian naphtha prices erased Tuesday's gains as the prompt physical market continues to pressure prices, traders said on Wednesday.
Some enquiries were heard from Japan but South Korean buyers were mostly at the sidelines, unhurried to cover their requirements, traders said.
Currrent premiums in Japan were at a discount of $2.30-$3.00 per tonne over Japan spot quotes, reflective of a bearish prompt market, traders said.
Premiums in Singapore were assessed at 40 cents free-on-board.
Some said the price fall is also triggered by sharp losses seen in the crude market.
The market was also distracted by the Saudi Aramco term talks with offers heard firm at $17-$17.50 for A-180 paraffinic naphtha and at $15.00 for full range naphtha loading from Jubail and Rabigh.
In the naphtha swaps market, both June and July fell 30 cents to $21.40/$21.60.
In the mogas market, a 92-octane cargo was offered at $23.65, slightly lower from the $23.70 offered on Tuesday.
Thailand's Rayong has also issued a tender to sell 200,000 barrel of 95-octance supplies for May loading.
Majors who have submitted prices said most bids were mostly at a discount between $1.00-$1.70, lower than Caltex Star refiner's earlier awards at minus 75 cents.
